messages:
zara: hey folks, first week q. cloned the repo into iCloud Drive (~/Library/Mobile Documents/...) and ran `docker compose up`. Postgres init fails with lots of permission errors: "initdb: could not create directory \"/var/lib/postgresql/data/pg_wal\": Permission denied" and then container exits.

mika: welcome! quick note: networked/cloud-synced folders (iCloud/Dropbox/OneDrive) and macOS metadata layers often don't support unix permissions or can lock files. Did you bind-mount a host dir into the container for pgdata?

zara: yep compose has `./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. I thought keeping the project in iCloud would be convenient but apparently not.

pablo: yup that's the issue. Those sync services intercept file operations and can hold locks or strip exec bits. Two easy fixes: 1) move the repo to a local path (e.g., ~/code) that is not synced, 2) use a named Docker volume instead of binding a host folder, e.g. `volumes: dbdata:` then `db: volumes: - dbdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`.

zara: moved the repo to ~/code and restarted. Postgres starts now. For posterity: logs showed multiple EACCES and then `initdb: removing contents of data directory \"/var/lib/postgresql/data\"` which was scary.

mika: another tip: if you must keep the repo on a synced folder, avoid bind-mounting the DB data dir to it. You can keep source files there but configure compose to use a named volume for DB. Also macOS Spotlight or antivirus can sometimes hold files open; exclude the project dir if you see weird hangs.

zara: good call. I'll update my onboarding notes: 1) do not run DB data dirs on cloud-synced mounts, 2) prefer named volumes or local non-synced paths, 3) if hitting weird permission/EACCES errors, check for sync services/Spotlight/AV.

infra-bot: Dev-setup doc updated with a note: "Avoid placing project DB data on cloud-synced folders (iCloud/Dropbox/OneDrive). Use local filesystem or named Docker volumes for Postgres to prevent permission and file-lock issues." https://go.redwood/dev-setup (:book:)

zara: thanks all! saved me a headache on day 2 :relieved:
